Siemens Digital Industries Software, Princeton, NJ, USA (single author)

Compares; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — controlled experiment: 5 informationally equivalent architecture specification formats x 6 models, 90 trials, plus a no-architecture baseline; hybrid evaluation (automated static checking + LLM-as-judge + process metrics) listed as a contribution

Five architecture specification formats (no SDD tool): (1) Prose (control); (2) Mermaid diagrams + numbered constraints + ADRs + route table; (3) OpenAPI 3.0 + Mermaid + constraints; (4) C4 / Structurizr DSL + Mermaid container diagram + constraints + ADRs; (5) TypeScript interface contracts + ArchUnit-style rules (pseudo-code). Baseline: requirements only, no architecture (Sonnet 4.6 only). Versions: OpenAPI 3.0; others Not stated

One architecture specification document per format, all encoding the same 7 elements: 7 components, communication patterns (event bus pub/sub), data ownership, 6 behavioral constraints, 25 HTTP routes, 3 ADRs (design rationale), prescribed file structure. Format-specific artefacts as listed under Approach

Single multi-turn session per trial: agent receives the specification and an identical implementation prompt, then iteratively writes files, compiles (tsc), fixes errors, runs a demo, signals done. No separate spec/plan/tasks phases
None during trials (autonomous agent; specifications authored by the author beforehand and reviewed for information equivalence)
Specification format only (architecture spec given as static context to a custom agent harness)

Not classifiable (no SDD workflow: a human-authored architecture specification is given once as static context before generation and not maintained; closest to spec-first). Authors' wording: 'architecture specification', 'specification as implementation interface', specs should be 'compilable, not merely parseable'
New project (greenfield): each trial starts from a clean directory
One reference system: Task Management API, 7 components, 25 routes, 6 constraints, 3 ADRs; generated code mean ~590-1,504 LOC per model (Sonnet 1,504 LOC, 14.3 files; Gemini Flash 590 LOC, 9.7 files)
Backend REST API (task management), TypeScript on Node.js built-in http, in-memory storage, no npm dependencies
N/A (no human participants; autonomous agent)
Total tokens per trial (proxy for API cost); agent turns; score per 100K tokens. No money or wall-clock time
API route coverage (% of 25 routes with a handler); TypeScript compilation pass rate; demo run (no functional acceptance test suite)

LLM-judge scores 1-10 (Sonnet 4.6, blind to format): architectural adherence, completeness, code quality, constraint compliance, overall; automated constraint violations (static import analysis); weighted architecture compliance score (components 20%, communication 20%, constraints 20%, routes 20%, data ownership 10%, file structure 10%; ~80% of the architecture machine-verifiable); LOC
None

Process metrics: tsc attempts and pass rate, demo run rate (self-validation), tool-call errors, file rewrite rate (debugging intensity); failure-mode taxonomy (compilation death spiral, premature termination, perfectionist iteration); judge-automation correlation, inter-judge agreement (GPT-5 re-judging), same-family bias

Automatic: harness logs (tokens, turns, tsc, demo, writes), static import analysis, route coverage script. LLM-as-judge (Claude Sonnet 4.6) for the four quality dimensions; 30 trials re-judged by GPT-5. No human scoring

Agent = custom TypeScript harness (tools write_file, read_file, list_files, run_command, done; max 50 turns, 16,384 output tokens/turn, default temperature) for all. Success criterion: none stated by the authors; metrics: judge overall (1-10), route coverage, compliance; 3 trials per cell. Per-model mean tokens (all formats, Table IX): Sonnet 640K, GPT-5 248K, Gemini Pro 329K, Haiku 735K, GPT-5-mini 225K, Gemini Flash 223K

Task: one reference system (Task Management API). Configurations: 5 formats x 6 models (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5; GPT-5, GPT-5-mini; Gemini 2.5 Pro, 2.5 Flash) = 30 cells, 90 trials, run as six sequential rounds; plus no-architecture baseline (Sonnet, 3 trials). Baseline: prose (control) for format; requirements-only for the premise. Held constant: information content of specs, implementation prompt, harness and tools, max turns/tokens, default temperature, clean directory, judge model (Sonnet 4.6). Acceptance tests: none functional; route coverage, static compliance and LLM judge. Repetitions: 3 per cell. Human intervention: none

Format x model interaction: format spread (max-min overall) Sonnet 0.17, GPT-5 0.92, GPT-5-mini 0.83, Haiku 1.67, Gemini Flash 1.08, Gemini Pro 2.42 (driven by TS 4.50). Best format varies: Mermaid (Sonnet), TS contracts (GPT-5), OpenAPI (Haiku, Gemini Pro), C4 (Gemini Flash); structured formats beat prose on Haiku, GPT-5-mini and Gemini Flash, but not on Gemini Pro, where TS contracts (4.50) is below prose (5.83), against the paper's claim that all structured formats outperform prose on smaller models. TS contracts the only format with 100% route coverage and compliance on all six models; Gemini Flash routes 33% (prose) -> 100% (TS). Architecture guidance vs none: +3.34 overall (5.08 -> 8.42). Cost: prose cheapest on Sonnet (433K vs 1,060K Mermaid); Haiku uses more tokens than Sonnet (735K vs 640K) for 1.9 points lower. Demo run rate 100% (Sonnet) to 0% (Gemini Flash). Significance: not tested (n = 3 per cell, stated as exploratory)

Distinguished configurations on weaker models (judge spreads, route coverage) but not on frontier models (Sonnet spread 0.17 within noise; within-condition variance exceeds between-condition on Sonnet). Repeatable: 3 trials/cell; harness and all 93 transcripts released; rounds run sequentially (temporal confound). Judge validated: Sonnet vs GPT-5 r = 0.47-0.60, GPT-5 +0.42 more lenient, no same-family bias; judge vs automated compliance r = 0.21. Limitations stated: underpowered, no significance tests, single system, same author wrote all specs, LLM-judge construct validity

n = 3 per cell, no statistical tests; one system of moderate complexity (~7 components); only proprietary models; all specifications written by the same author; sequential rounds (API load, model updates); LLM judge not validated against humans, possible same-family bias; formats like UML, SysML v2, AADL, Terraform not tested. Future: capability continuum, hybrid formats, larger systems (10+ services), variance reduction, constraint checking in the agent loop, incremental development by a second agent

Data and harness public: github.com/arquicanedo/architecture-as-equalizer (93 transcripts, codebases, specs, judge scores). No pre-registration. Language: TypeScript. Agent is a custom harness, not a commercial agent; model versions without snapshot dates. Inconsistencies: Haiku overall 6.50 in text and Table IX vs 6.55 in Table V; GPT-5-mini 6.72 (Table IX) vs 6.68 (Table V); format effect '10x larger on the smaller model' (p. 2, Sonnet vs Haiku) vs 'up to 14x' (p. 5); paper says specs 'written by the same authors' though single author; text says 'all structured formats outperform prose on smaller models' (p. 5), but Table V gives Gemini Pro TS contracts 4.50 < prose 5.83.
